newsitem.title: UK: US equity fund inflows face declines - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: US equity fund inflows face declines - JP Morgan.

text.p: A 25 basis point hike in U.S. interest rates in March and the recent equity market consolidation may put a brake on near term inflows into U.S. equity funds, JP Morgan said in a report on global fund flows.

It said February fund flow data from the U.S. already showed a diversification of portfolios, with international and global funds together accounting for a record 11 percent of fund assets at the end of the month.

Also, a rising U.S. long bond yield could prompt a further asset allocation shift. "It will be interesting to see if there is an asset allocation shift from equities in favour of cash or bonds," the report said.
Fund tracking firm AMG Data Services said on Friday U.S. equity mutual funds suffered their first redemptions of the year for the week ending April 2, with redemptions of $328 million for the week.
US domestic equity funds attracted less net inflows in February following strong inflows in the previous two months, the JP Morgan report said.
It said net subscriptions to domestic U.S. equity funds slowed to $14.5 billion in February from over $24 billion in both December and January.
Net inflows into international funds also slowed, although to a lesser extent as they attracted $3 billion, or 15.7 percent of total inflows.
In terms of sectors, it said technology and energy saw some heavy selling, while healthcare attracted new investment.
